issues.where: tabletop and plinth, 1.50–1.73 s; see also set-D-01.jpg, 2.40–2.77 s
issues.what: The wood and tabletop flash orange as the large winter snow patches vanish, then the patches visibly grow back from the base after touchdown. The outdoor powder changes more conspicuously than the globe lands.
issues.fix: Keep the winter plinth and tabletop snow continuous through the test shake. If powder is disturbed, displace and redeposit the same visible material instead of clearing and restoring its coverage with a timed fade.

issues.where: lower rim and contact shadow, 0.40–0.57 s; see also set-C-02.jpg at touchdown
issues.what: The globe glides sideways on an almost level lift and eases into contact with little visible load transfer. The strokes do have clear reversals, but the endpoints make the plinth feel light.
issues.fix: Peel one rim edge off the table before the other, then land one edge first with a brief damped rock and a tighter contact shadow at impact.

issues.where: lower half of the glass during the first second after landing
issues.what: The storm clearly outlasts the glass motion, but the brightest snow remains a broad smear across the lower glass as the tree reappears. The end reads more as the mist thinning than distinct flakes slowing and settling.
issues.fix: Retain the coherent residual whirl but break the lower smear into depth-separated flakes that visibly descend and accumulate on the ground and miniature as the circulation slows.
